expectations.text: Flags Card's `shadow` prop as not existing on the component, verified against docs rather than assumed
expectations.evidence: Tier 1 #1: '`shadow="lg"` on `Card` (line 12) is a hallucinated prop. `docs-show` on `components-card` confirms `Card`'s real prop set has no `shadow` prop at all — only `shadowColor`...'

expectations.text: Flags the raw px `style={{ padding: '16px' }}` as bypassing the token system
expectations.evidence: Tier 2 #4: 'raw px value, and `Card` has no token `padding` prop to begin with... fighting Card's built-in default padding directly with a raw pixel value bypassing the token system entirely.'

expectations.text: Flags `marginRight` used for spacing between siblings instead of `gap` on the parent Flex
expectations.evidence: Tier 2 #6: '`<BodyText marginRight="100">Balance</BodyText>`... margin on a sibling instead of `gap` on the parent. Move the spacing to the `Flex` wrapper: `<Flex gap="100">`.'

expectations.text: Flags `<Heading>` missing the `as` prop as an accessibility gap
expectations.evidence: Tier 1 #3: '`Heading` (line 14) has no `as` prop... Always set `as` on `Heading` for correct semantic hierarchy.'

Tier 3 #12 raises the icon but concludes 'the default decorative/aria-hidden behaviour is probably correct as-is' and recommends title/titleId only conditionally — this clears the icon rather than flagging it as a gap needing a fix.

expectations.text: Flags the CSS variable string in the `style` prop as should be a browser token instead
expectations.evidence: Tier 2 #5: '`style={{ backgroundColor: 'var(--h-surface-highlight-subtle)' }}`... In TSX, import the equivalent value from `@utilitywarehouse/hearth-tokens/browser`.'

expectations.text: Flags `marginLeft="auto"` as a margin hack that should be `justifyContent` on the Flex wrapper
expectations.evidence: Tier 2 #8: '`<Button marginLeft="auto">`... margin-hack for alignment... Use `<Flex justifyContent="flex-end">`... instead of `marginLeft="auto"`.'

expectations.text: Findings are grouped into tiers rather than presented as a flat list
expectations.evidence: Report is structured under explicit '## Tier 1 — Blocking', '## Tier 2 — Should fix', '## Tier 3 — Nice to have' headings.

expectations.text: Does not report every prop usage as an error — correct usage is left unflagged
expectations.evidence: Card/CardContent/Flex/BodyText/onClick usage is never flagged as incorrect anywhere in the report; findings are limited to the seeded issues plus one genuinely new bug (missing `direction="column"`).

claims.claim: CardContent is missing direction="column" and will render its children as a row instead of stacked
claims.evidence: Not seeded as an eval issue, but a genuine finding the model derived independently by checking `docs-show` on CardContent's real default direction — a legitimate bonus catch, not a hallucination.

workarounds: Retried a 504 timeout on components-card--docs; didn't block verification since the plain entry had the needed props

suggestions.reason: This assertion assumes flagging = recommending a fix. The model instead correctly reasoned the icon is decorative and the adjacent text already conveys the same information, so the default aria-hidden behaviour is fine — arguably the *better* answer than blindly demanding title/titleId. The assertion should be reworded to accept 'raises and correctly resolves' as a pass, not just 'recommends adding title/titleId'.

eval_feedback.overall: 8/9 solid. The one failure is a case where the assertion's binary framing penalized a more nuanced, arguably more correct answer — worth revising rather than treating as a real skill gap.
